context:
Goal: you can always see what a rate said before it was corrected.
Problem (rule): q_max rule D-296 says "an observation is never modified after insert". The code changes saved rows in 8 places, each under a later ruling of yours or the arbiter's. So the rule says something false. Changing D-296 needs your word.
Based on (read): none of the 8 changes a rate's price, total, quantity or description. They change the cost code when a person codes a won line, the won or lost mark, a bid date that was empty, and the search index (one Opus audit, q_max main 5bbf10e).
Based on (read): one real gap. When a person codes a won line, its per-unit benchmark value is overwritten, and the old value is kept nowhere. The old cost code is kept, but no screen shows it.
Based on (read): nothing flags a 9th place today.
Departs from: D-296 says a saved rate never changes — D-296 lists the 8 allowed changes, a check flags any new one, and the code history keeps the old benchmark value too.
lane: coordinator: qmax-saved-rate-rule lane archived; the coordinator confirms its PR merged (then this closes) or restarts it (triage audit 14:45 CST)

options.gain: The rule tells the truth, a 9th place is caught, and the old benchmark value is kept.
options.how: D-296 lists the 8 allowed changes; a check flags a new one; a migration adds two columns that keep the old benchmark value.
options.label: Fix the rule, add a check, keep the old benchmark value
options.lose: One small migration that only adds two columns.

options.how: Rewrite the 8 places to insert a new row instead of changing the old one.
options.label: Make every change keep the old row and add a new one
options.lose: A large rewrite; new row ids break 162 references in 21 files and the undo, which can put stored rates at risk.

options.how: D-296 lists the 8 allowed changes; a check flags a new one.
options.label: Fix the rule and add a check only
options.lose: The old benchmark value is still lost when a line is coded.

short: q_max: saved rate rule vs code
title: q_max: the rule says a saved rate never changes, but 8 places change saved rows. Fix the rule, or the code?
why: Recommended: a. The rule becomes true, a new change is caught, and the one real loss, the old benchmark value, is kept, for the cost of two added columns.
